title: CFTC Commitments of Traders (COT) report data, as futures-market context
description: Ch. 37's Commitments of Traders report is the one genuinely new, freely available data source in that chapter: the CFTC publishes weekly long/short positioning by commercials/large speculators/small speculators for every futures market, publicly and for free. Elder's own framing: follow commercials (historically successful), fade small speculators (historically unsuccessful), read current positioning against historical norms. This is a futures-market indicator, informational context (e.g. for the ch.57 daily-homework idea's gold/oil/currency-futures lines) -- not something that plugs into any per-stock-ticker signal the way insider clusters or short interest do. Scoped to a small, informational surface only.

checklist.step: Research the CFTC's actual public data format/endpoint for COT reports (it's a public government dataset -- confirm the concrete access mechanism, e.g. a downloadable file or an API) and record findings as a decisions entry.
Implement a minimal fetch of current + recent positioning for a small, fixed set of major futures markets (e.g. Euro, Yen, Oil, Gold, Bonds -- matching the ch.57 daily-homework idea's own list).
Decide where this surfaces (a new small, standalone endpoint; explicitly not wired into any per-stock-ticker signal) and record the decision.
Unit tests mocking the data source.

decisions.decision: CFTC's Commitments of Traders data is accessed via the CFTC's own public Socrata Open Data (SODA) JSON API, specifically the "Legacy" report's "Futures Only" dataset at `https://publicreporting.cftc.gov/resource/6dca-aqww.json` -- confirmed live during this task (a plain HTTP GET, no auth/API key required for this app's low request volume; Socrata offers an optional app token purely for higher rate limits, not needed here). Confirmed field mapping: `market_and_exchange_names`/`cftc_contract_market_code` identify one specific futures contract, `report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd` is the report's as-of Tuesday (reports are released the following Friday), and `noncomm_positions_long_all`/`noncomm_positions_short_all` (CFTC's "Non-Commercial" = Elder's large speculators), `comm_positions_long_all`/`comm_positions_short_all` (commercials), `nonrept_positions_long_all`/`nonrept_positions_short_all` (CFTC's "Non-Reportable" = Elder's small speculators), and `open_interest_all` are exactly the fields Elder's ch. 37 three-way breakdown needs.
decisions.rationale: The Legacy/Futures-Only report was chosen over the CFTC's newer 'Disaggregated' and 'Traders in Financial Futures' (TFF) reports specifically because it's the classic three-way Commercial/Non-Commercial/Non-Reportable split Elder's own ch. 37 text describes; the newer reports split those same groups further (e.g. producer/merchant vs. swap dealer for Disaggregated, dealer/asset-manager/leveraged-money/other for TFF), which is more granular detail than this app's minimal scope needs and would require reinterpreting which sub-group(s) map onto Elder's 'commercials'/'large speculators'. The Socrata JSON API was chosen over the CFTC's alternative plain-text/CSV weekly bulletin downloads (e.g. `cftc.gov/dea/newcot/FinFutWk.txt`, confirmed also live and public) because it's directly queryable (filter by contract code, date-ordered, limited) rather than requiring this app to parse CFTC's fixed-width/CSV historical-bulletin format itself, and because a single compound `cftc_contract_market_code IN (...)` filter can fetch every one of this task's 5 fixed markets' trailing history in one HTTP request instead of five separate downloads.

decisions.decision: The 5 fixed futures markets (matching the ch. 57 daily-homework idea's own Euro/Yen/Oil/Gold/Bonds list) map to these specific CFTC `cftc_contract_market_code` values, each confirmed live against the Socrata endpoint (most recent `report_date_as_yyyy_mm_dd` returned, non-stale) as of this task's original research (2026-09-22): eur=099741 (EURO FX - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE), jpy=097741 (JAPANESE YEN - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE), oil=067651 (CRUDE OIL, LIGHT SWEET/WTI - NEW YORK MERCANTILE EXCHANGE), gold=088691 (GOLD - COMMODITY EXCHANGE INC.), bonds=020601 (U.S. TREASURY BONDS - CHICAGO BOARD OF TRADE). NOTE (added by backend-cftc-cot-data-followups, same day): the `cftc_contract_market_code` values themselves are still correct/live and unaffected, but the parenthetical display names above are illustrative-only and have already drifted for two of the five -- CFTC has since renamed both oil (067651, live endpoint now returns "WTI-PHYSICAL - NEW YORK MERCANTILE EXCHANGE") and bonds (020601, live endpoint now returns "UST BOND - CHICAGO BOARD OF TRADE"). The endpoint's own `market_and_exchange_names` response field is always populated live, never hardcoded, so this never affected app behavior -- treat these parentheticals as a snapshot of the name at research time, not a fact that stays true, and don't use them to cross-check a live query without expecting possible drift.
decisions.rationale: Several of these commodities have multiple CFTC-tracked contracts across different exchanges for the same underlying (e.g. NYMEX WTI light-sweet crude vs. ICE's Brent/WTI-Financial variants; CBOT's plain, 'Long Term', and 'Ultra' Treasury Bond contracts). Rather than surfacing all of them (which would turn a fixed 5-entry response into an open-ended list this app's minimal scope doesn't need) or guessing from the contract name alone, each code was picked as the single most standard/commonly-referenced US-exchange contract for that commodity, and its liveness was verified by querying the endpoint directly during this task rather than assumed.

decisions.decision: Elder's 'read current positioning against historical norms' framing is operationalized via the classic Williams 'COT Index' formula: `(current_net - min(history_net)) / (max(history_net) - min(history_net)) * 100`, computed separately for each of commercial/large-speculator/small-speculator net positions over a trailing 52-week window (including the current week itself, per that indicator's standard definition). Returned as `commercial_cot_index_52w`/`large_speculator_cot_index_52w`/`small_speculator_cot_index_52w` on `GET /api/cftc/cot`, null when fewer than 2 weeks of history exist or the window's range is zero-width (an undefined case, not defaulted to a misleading 50/neutral).
decisions.rationale: A raw net-position count (long minus short) isn't meaningfully comparable across time on its own, since overall open interest/market size grows and shrinks -- Elder's own text explicitly calls for reading positioning 'against historical norms', not an absolute level. The Williams COT Index is the standard, well-known way this specific normalization is done for COT data (rather than inventing a bespoke percentile-rank scheme), so it was used directly instead. 52 weeks (~1 trading year) was chosen as the window over other common choices (26/156 weeks) as a reasonable middle ground requiring no extra history-length configuration; this can be revisited in a follow-up if a specific different window length is ever wanted.

decisions.decision: This surfaces as a new, standalone `GET /api/cftc/cot` endpoint (`app/api/routers/cftc.py`) returning all 5 fixed markets' current + recent positioning in one response -- not wired into `app.signals`/`app.portfolio` or any per-stock-ticker analysis endpoint in any way. `CFTCCOTProvider` is injected via a plain per-request `get_cftc_cot_provider` FastAPI dependency (a fresh, stateless instance each call, mirroring `get_data_provider`'s yfinance/Stooq construction) rather than a process-wide singleton like `get_ibkr_provider`'s, and the endpoint always fetches fresh from CFTC on every request with no local DB-backed cache/persistence layer (unlike `CachedDataProvider`'s OHLCV/extended-data caches or `IBKRBreadthSnapshotORM`'s once-per-day snapshot table).
decisions.rationale: The task's own description is explicit that this is 'informational context... not something that plugs into any per-stock-ticker signal', so no route/module in app.signals or app.portfolio references it, matching how IBKR's market-scanner/breadth features are also kept out of the signal engine. No singleton is needed because `CFTCCOTProvider` (unlike `IBKRProvider`) has no per-instance rate-limit/session/cache state to preserve across requests -- constructing it fresh per call costs nothing. No DB cache was added because the task's checklist scopes this to 'a minimal fetch' and the underlying CFTC data only changes weekly regardless of how often this app's own endpoint is called; adding a caching layer (e.g. a new ORM table keyed by market+report_date, mirroring `IBKRBreadthSnapshotORM`) is a reasonable follow-up if this endpoint turns out to be called often enough that repeated CFTC round-trips matter, but was left out here as an unnecessary complication for a first, minimal version.

decisions.decision: Fixed the pr-reviewer needs_work blocking finding (PR #270 review): `CFTCCOTProvider.get_all_recent()`'s row-grouping step now wraps `row['cftc_contract_market_code']` in a try/except (`KeyError`, `TypeError`) that raises `DataProviderUnavailableError`, matching `_to_report()`'s own established convention a few lines below, instead of letting a bare `KeyError` escape past the router's `except DataProviderUnavailableError` handler as an unhandled 500. Added a unit regression test (`TestGetAllRecent.test_row_missing_contract_code_raises_data_provider_unavailable`) and an integration-level regression test reproducing the reviewer's exact repro (`test_malformed_cftc_row_returns_503_not_500`: real `CFTCCOTProvider` with `_request` patched to return a row missing the key, hit `GET /api/cftc/cot`, assert 503) since the existing integration tests all stub `get_all_recent()` itself and so couldn't have caught this. Did not touch the non-blocking oil/bonds display-name documentation finding from the same review -- that's tracked separately as the `backend-cftc-cot-data-followups` task per the review comment.
decisions.rationale: TypeError (not just KeyError) is also caught because a malformed CFTC response could plausibly return a non-dict row (e.g. a bare string or list entry) in the same slot, which would raise TypeError rather than KeyError on subscript access -- consistent with `_to_report`'s own broader except clause a few lines below in the same file, and cheap to include defensively rather than leaving a second, narrower bare-exception gap right next to the one just fixed.

comments.summary: Round 1 blocking finding (CFTCCOTProvider.get_all_recent() bare KeyError -> unhandled 500 instead of documented 503) is fixed: the row-grouping step now wraps row['cftc_contract_market_code'] in try/except (KeyError, TypeError), raising DataProviderUnavailableError, matching _to_report()'s own established convention. Independently re-verified by checking out the pre-fix commit (b7dfabb) into a scratch worktree, dropping in the new integration test unmodified, and confirming it fails there with the exact same uncaught KeyError round 1 reported; against the current fixed code the same test passes with a 503. The new integration test (test_malformed_cftc_row_returns_503_not_500) uses the real CFTCCOTProvider via the dependency override rather than the existing tests' _StubCFTCCOTProvider (which bypasses get_all_recent's own grouping logic), so it genuinely exercises the fixed code path. The added TypeError catch is sound, not overly broad: a non-dict row (bare string/list) in the response would raise TypeError rather than KeyError on subscript access, and _to_report's own broader except clause a few lines below already catches the same TypeError case for the same reason.

Non-blocking: the decisions entry recording the 5 cftc_contract_market_code values, and the matching COT_MARKETS inline comments, give market_and_exchange_names display text for oil (067651) and bonds (020601) that no longer matches what the live CFTC Socrata endpoint returns today (oil: 'CRUDE OIL, LIGHT SWEET (WTI) - NEW YORK MERCANTILE EXCHANGE' recorded vs. live 'WTI-PHYSICAL - NEW YORK MERCANTILE EXCHANGE'; bonds: 'U.S. TREASURY BONDS - CHICAGO BOARD OF TRADE' recorded vs. live 'UST BOND - CHICAGO BOARD OF TRADE'). Confirmed via live query + historical lookback that CFTC renamed both contracts at some point; the contract codes themselves are correct and still live, and the endpoint's own display_name field is always populated from the live response (never hardcoded), so this is a documentation-accuracy nit only, not a functional bug. Already tracked on backend-cftc-cot-data-followups (still planned) -- not duplicated here.
